title: Slow Order API
description: Order API latency rose from 180 ms to 4.2 s. Error rate is stable and there was no deploy.

nodes.text: Order API latency rose from 180 ms to 4.2 s. Error rate is stable and there was no deploy.

actions.label: Inspect slow queries
actions.result: One SELECT averages 3.8 seconds and accounts for most database time.

actions.label: Restart application
actions.result: Queues clear and latency drops briefly. Four minutes later it reaches 5.1 s; 17 sessions were disconnected.

nodes.text: The incident continues. Temporary relief did not address the underlying cause.
observations: Queues clear and latency drops briefly. Four minutes later it reaches 5.1 s; 17 sessions were disconnected.
The team still needs a diagnosis.

actions.label: Inspect slow queries
actions.result: One SELECT averages 3.8 seconds and accounts for most database time.

nodes.text: The first evidence narrows the fault domain.
observations: One SELECT averages 3.8 seconds and accounts for most database time.

actions.label: Examine execution plan
actions.result: The plan shows a full scan of ORDER_ITEM; estimated and actual rows diverge sharply.

actions.label: Create the reviewed index without verification
actions.result: The unverified change creates risk and the incident is escalated after the recovery window expires.

nodes.text: Evidence now supports a specific root cause.
observations: The plan shows a full scan of ORDER_ITEM; estimated and actual rows diverge sharply.

actions.label: Create the reviewed index
actions.result: The online index build completes. Latency settles at 190 ms without errors.

nodes.text: Service indicators remain healthy through the observation window.
observations: The online index build completes. Latency settles at 190 ms without errors.

nodes.text: The response window closes with customer impact unresolved.
observations: The incident is handed to the next response team.

rootCause: An unusable index on ORDER_ITEM.ORDER_ID caused full table scans as data grew.

review.explanation: An unusable index on ORDER_ITEM.ORDER_ID caused full table scans as data grew.
learningNotes: Use evidence to narrow the fault domain before changing production.
Temporary symptom relief is not the same as removing a root cause.
